key_insight: An explainable ML pipeline can learn a closed-form inductance equation that generalizes far better than conventional black-box models for multilayer planar windings.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more reliable inductance estimation for high-frequency power converter design, reducing dependence on expensive FEM sweeps and rigid empirical formulas.
method: Post-hoc explainability with SHAP and permutation importance to rank influential winding features.
SR-KAN symbolic regression to discover an analytical expression without assuming a predefined formula form.
Validation on both large OOD FEM cases and physical PCB prototypes.
evidence_signal: The study used over 10,000 FEA simulations across seven OOD classes and 55 PCB prototypes, with SR-KAN reaching 8.22% OOD relative error and 6.26% mean absolute relative error on hardware.
watch_item: The discovered formula is data-driven and should still be checked carefully when moving to winding geometries or materials beyond the reported dataset.
paper_title: Explainable Machine Learning for Multilayer Planar Winding Inductance Estimation
